method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill (and references/regulative.md), from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the rulings on negatives of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05 (JUST FALSE where the text says no, NOTHING with a NOTHING-kind tag where it does not answer); dates in a small module, the rules in one module and the survivor's questions in a seat module importing it; two regulative rules (the s 5A(3) time bar and the s 5C(5) bar on recovery) run by EVALTRACE inside exported questions that take only plain facts; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. A second encoding beside baseline-2026-11 (the claimant's whole-Act baseline, untouched), focused on the child abuse provisions. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
focus: Tasmania's equivalents of the child abuse limitation removals and organisational liability amendments: in this Act s 5B (no limitation period) and s 5C (setting aside settlements), with ss 5A, 26(1A), 26A, 38, 38A and 39(1) around them; the organisational liability half is Part 10C of the Civil Liability Act 2002 (Tas), a different Act, out of this folder
edition_encoded: Limitation Act 1974 (Tas), No. 98 of 1974, consolidated version published 2024-07-18 and current at point in time 2026-11-06, as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/act-1974-098.txt (text sha256 af438489217489f460ca4175f4164883be2802db4d16f65989fd487676fada09), retrieved from legislation.tas.gov.au on 2026-11-06

seat: the survivor: the person sexually or physically abused as a child who brings or proposes to bring an action for damages for the injury, or after the survivor's death the family member or personal representative bringing a Fatal Accidents Act 1934 action (tlca-seat.l4)

checks.l4: stable l4 of VS Code extension legalese.l4-vscode 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset
checks.command: l4 run tlca-dates.l4 ; l4 run tlca-rules.l4 ; l4 run tlca-seat.l4 ; l4 run tlca-cases.l4
checks.result: 89 assertions written, 89 satisfied, 0 errors, 0 warnings in every file (2026-11-07)
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics were read; satisfied assertions were counted by distinct source range. Expected values worked by hand from the text.

scope: In: ss 2(1) (date of discoverability, as input), 5A(3)-(5) for abuse outside s 5B, 5B, 5C(1)-(8), 26(1A), 26A(1)-(5), 38, 38A(1)-(3), 39(1). Out: Civil Liability Act 2002 (Tas) Part 10C and s 4(9) (a different Act); the rest of this Act (in baseline-2026-11); ss 5A(6), 32, 26A(6), (7) and a second suspension spell (in baseline-2026-11); ss 38A(4), 39(2) (actions already begun). Reasons in NOTES.md.
